newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African golds end firm, Greenspan hits industrials.
newsitem.headline: S.African golds end firm, Greenspan hits industrials.

text.p: South African gold shares, helped by a weaker rand and a firmer bullion price sparkled towards the close of Thursday's mixed trading session, dealers said.

Industrials limped for most of the day after an overnight dive of Wall Street, a weaker rand and nervousness over hawkish comments by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan late on Wednesday, they said.
Greenspan warned on Wednesday that U.S. stock prices may have risen too far and hinted that the Federal Reserve could hike U.S. interest rates.

The gold index ended the day 44.6 points higher -- nearly three percent -- at 1,588.1 while the industrial index sagged 55.1 points to 8,323.7, leaving the overall share index 10.0 points lower at 7,195.7.

The bullion price -- which at the start of the week hovered around the $352 level per ounce -- moved up to $360 per ounce, with dealers commenting that most buyers had seen the yellow metal as the day's choice on Thursday.

Dealers said the market discounted most of the economic data released on Thursday, including trade, GDP and inflation figures but would be closely watching January money supply data for direction on Friday.

But preliminary Reserve Bank figures released at 1500 GMT on Thursday -- after the official stock market close -- showed South Africa's year-on-year broadly defined M3 money supply grew 16.89 percent in January, far above a Reuters consensus forecast of 15.8 percent.
